title: Choose the visual world for the KAMI dashboard
question: The roll assigned Tank Band. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. (You were away; Claude builds the assigned direction unless you pick another here.)

options.label: Tank Band
options.lineage: painted municipal overhead water tanks with stencilled ward numbers, Tamil Nadu
options.thesis: Every sensor point wears its tank band: a stencilled ward number on a painted band whose colour and pattern are its state.
options.viewport: Municipal-blue header with tabs, replay strip, the map with band markers left, four status bands and the live alert register right; the top alert alone on a reversed plate.
options.risk: Stencil type turns into an industrial costume if it leaves the numbers.

raised.raise: Poster-scale type ramp: the node number is stencilled at poster size on its own page, caption-size everywhere else.
Rank by weight, case and reversal: only the single most urgent alert is set on a reversed plate.
Nothing disappears, it cancels: closed alerts stay in the register, struck with a CLOSED mark.
Registration: the four signal charts share one time axis and one onset mark.
One subject owns the node page: the node's band, number and state lead it.

options.label: Network Drawing
options.lineage: PWD / TWAD water-supply network drawings, diazo prints
options.thesis: The network as the department's own drawing: diazo-blue lines, a title block per node, red-pencil revisions for alerts.
options.viewport: Drawing-sheet ground, the map as the drawing, a title-block schedule of 8 nodes right, alerts as red revision clouds.
options.risk: Blueprint is where most 'technical' redesigns land; familiar rather than new.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.lineage: spectrogram plates on a viewing box
options.thesis: State as line form, not hue: each node's evidence drawn as hairlines on one calibrated rail.
options.viewport: Charcoal ground, the map left, a rail of 8 nodes right where solid, dashed, half-height and doubled lines carry state.
options.case: Holds clarity (state encoded twice, by form and colour); operators do not know spectrograms.
options.risk: Dark, abstract and quiet; may read as lab equipment.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.thesis: Giant lowercase type and colour tiles as the interface.
options.case: Loses both: operators do not identify with it and tiles bury the map.
options.kept: Poster-scale type ramp for the node number.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One node per screen, flick to the next.
options.case: Loses both: an operator needs the whole network at once.
options.kept: One subject owns the node page.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case, reversal and rule.
options.case: Loses both: the rake and single size slow reading.
options.kept: Only the most urgent alert gets a reversed plate.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Same scale and ground on every plate.
options.case: Loses both: no link to water operations.
options.kept: Registration: charts share one time axis and onset mark.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: States stamp themselves; nothing disappears, it cancels.
options.risk: Airline nostalgia, foreign to the audience.
options.case: Loses both: no audience link; coupons hide the map.
options.kept: Closed alerts stay listed, struck with CLOSED.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean light operations dashboard: side navigation, white panels, one blue accent, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Side rail, KPI row, map and alert table in white panels.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every admin dashboard by design.
